subject: design-studies
title: Ergonomic Dimensions: Fit the Chair and Desk to the Student
objectives: Explain how ergonomic dimensions are set from the user measurements: seat height, seat width and desk height
Work the three sums for one student: seat height 40 cm, seat width 36 + 4 cm, desk height 40 + 24 cm
Explain why a chair built to average measurements leaves fit gaps for anyone who is not average

definitions.meaning: Designing a product around the measurements and needs of the user who will use it, so the product fits the person.
The height from the floor to the underside of the thigh when seated; it sets the seat height so the feet rest flat.
The width of the user hips; with clearance added, it sets the seat width.
The extra room added beyond a body measurement - here 4 cm added to the hip breadth so the seat is not a tight squeeze.
The height of the elbow above the seat when seated; added to the seat height, it sets the desk height so the forearms rest level.
The bar in the animation that climbs as each fit gap closes: one third for the seat height, two thirds after the width and desk height, full when every dimension fits.

mechanismSteps: Measure the student: lower-leg height 40 cm, hip breadth 36 cm, seated elbow 24 cm above the seat, and the fit bar starts empty (s1).
Set the seat height: it rises to the lower-leg height of 40 cm, the feet rest flat, the gap under the thigh closes, and the fit bar climbs to one third (s2).

Set the seat width and the desk height: the seat widens to hip breadth plus clearance (36 + 4 = 40 cm) and the desk top settles at seat height plus seated elbow height (40 + 24 = 64 cm), so the fit bar climbs to two thirds (s3).
The fitted sizes are restored after the standard-size wrong turn leaves feet dangling: seat, width and desk each set from the student own measurements, and the fit bar fills (s4).
workedExample: Work through the whole sizing in order. Measure first (s1): lower-leg height 40 cm, hip breadth 36 cm, seated elbow height 24 cm. Seat height (s2): set to the lower-leg height, 40 cm, so the feet rest flat. Seat width (s3): hip breadth plus clearance, 36 + 4 = 40 cm. Desk height (s3): seat height plus seated elbow height, 40 + 24 = 64 cm, so the forearms rest level. At every stage the order is the same: take a measurement of the user, then let that measurement set one dimension, and watch the fit bar climb as each gap closes.

trap.misconception: One standard size fits every user, because a chair built to average measurements fits each person who sits in it.
trap.explanation: The slip: A standard chair looks like it fits because most people can sit on it, so it is easy to assume the average size is close enough for every body. The fix: Ergonomic design sizes the product from the user's own measurements: the seat height is set to the lower-leg height so the feet rest flat, the seat width to the hip breadth plus clearance, and the desk height to the seat height plus the seated elbow height - a chair built to the average leaves every gap open for anyone who is not average. In class, replay scene 4: freeze on the standard chair with the feet dangling, then run the fitted sizes being restored and ask which measurement sets each dimension as the fit bar fills.
